description: Faction NPC dialogues triggered by moral threshold events. Each event fires once per save when the player crosses a moral band boundary overnight. These are the world acknowledging what you've become.

moral_event_bounty_issued.event_description: Fires when the player enters VeryEvil band (-100 or below). Peacekeepers issue a bounty.

peacekeeper_dialogue.speaker: Peacekeeper Sergeant Veill
lines: Your face is on the board now. I put it there myself.
You had a chance to be something other than this. That chance is spent.
The bounty is alive. For now. Push further and I cross out the 'alive' with my own hand.
Every patrol from here to the southern corridor knows your description. Height, gait, the scar. All of it.
Run if you want. Hide if you can. But know this: someone in this wasteland wants the rations that come with your capture.

peacekeeper_dialogue.speaker: Anonymous Peacekeeper recruit
lines: I saw the poster. Is that really you?
Look — I'm not going to try anything. I'm new. But the ones who aren't new? They're watching.
The sergeant says you're worse than the raiders. The raiders at least have a code.

raider_dialogue.speaker: Raider lookout, unnamed
lines: The Peacekeepers put a price on you. You know what that means to us?
It means you're interesting. And interesting people either trade with us or feed the dogs.
Relax. We don't collect Peacekeeper bounties. Bad for brand. But we respect the résumé.
You want to pass? You pass. Just know we're watching what you do with that freedom.

knowledge_keeper_dialogue.speaker: Knowledge Keeper archivist
lines: We record everything. You know that.
Your name has a page now. It's in the section between 'dangerous' and 'lost.' I'm not sure which side it'll land on.
The children ask about the bad names in the record. Yours came up yesterday.
I won't bar the door. Knowledge doesn't choose its subjects. But I'll watch my notes while you're here.

moral_event_bounty_issued.journal_entry: The Peacekeepers have issued a bounty with my face on it. The sergeant put it up himself. Every patrol knows my description now.

moral_event_contract_taken.event_description: Fires when the player enters Positive band (+50 to +99). Peacekeepers offer a standing contract — protection for cooperation.

peacekeeper_dialogue.speaker: Peacekeeper Captain Osa
lines: Sit. Please.
We've been watching you. Not the bad kind. The kind where we watch someone do good work and think: we could use that.
I'm offering you a contract. Not employment — a partnership. You keep doing what you're doing. We make sure the road stays clear for you.
The safehouses between here and the ridge? Open to you now. Patrols will nod, not draw.
You've earned something most people never earn out here: the benefit of the doubt. Don't spend it carelessly.

raider_dialogue.speaker: Raider captain, scarred woman
lines: I hear the Peacekeepers love you now. Contract and everything.
That means you're their problem, not ours. And problems get solved.
Don't come through our wire expecting the same welcome you used to get. The landscape changed.
We don't hate you. We just don't trust people who carry a Peacekeeper handshake.

knowledge_keeper_dialogue.speaker: Knowledge Keeper elder
lines: Your name appears in our records more often now. In the right section.
We've voted. You may access the restricted shelves. Not all of them. But more than most.
The world needs builders more than it needs scholars. You build well. Let us record what you build.

moral_event_contract_taken.journal_entry: The Peacekeepers offered me a contract — not employment, a partnership. Their safehouses are open to me now. Patrols nod instead of drawing.

moral_event_contract_raised.event_description: Fires when the player enters VeryPositive band (+100 or above). The contract deepens — the player becomes a recognized community figure.

peacekeeper_dialogue.speaker: Peacekeeper Captain Osa
lines: I need to tell you something, and I need you to hear it straight.
People follow you now. Not in the 'I'm walking behind you' way — in the 'I'd walk where you point' way.
That's power. The kind we can't issue from a badge. The kind that just... grows.
Your contract is raised. Full logistics support: medical, ammunition, passage through every corridor we hold.
But I'm going to ask you for something in return. Not now. Soon. And it won't be small.
You've become something the wasteland rarely produces. Don't let them turn you into a flag.

raider_dialogue.speaker: Raider lieutenant, young man with old eyes
lines: I know who you are. Everyone does.
My captain says to kill you on sight. Me? I think that's a waste.
You ever decide the Peacekeepers don't deserve you, come find us. We could use a real leader.
Until then — don't walk our roads at night. The order is the order, even if I disagree with it.

knowledge_keeper_dialogue.speaker: Knowledge Keeper council leader
lines: We don't often do this. Almost never, in fact.
We're offering you a seat at the long table. Not as a Keeper — as a witness. Your story, told in your words, preserved in our archive.
The world forgets everything eventually. Let us remember you correctly.
Come when you're ready. The chair will be there.

moral_event_contract_raised.journal_entry: The Peacekeepers raised my contract to full support — logistics, medical, passage through every corridor they hold. Captain Osa says I've become something the wasteland rarely produces. The Knowledge Keepers offered me a seat at their long table.

moral_event_patrol_defense.event_description: Fires alongside contract_raised at VeryPositive. Patrols actively defend the player's shelter.

peacekeeper_dialogue.speaker: Peacekeeper patrol leader
lines: Captain's orders. We're on rotation at your perimeter now.
Don't worry about the east approach — we've got eyes there from dusk to dawn.
Raiders tested us last week. They didn't test us twice.
You do what you do. We'll make sure you have a home to come back to.

raider_dialogue.speaker: Raider scout, crouching in brush
lines: The Peacekeepers posted a guard on your door. Makes hitting you complicated.
My crew isn't looking for a firefight with an armored squad.
We'll stay out of your yard for now. Just remember that guards change shifts.
Nobody stands sentry forever out here.

knowledge_keeper_dialogue.speaker: Knowledge Keeper observer
lines: A military perimeter around a civilian shelter is a rare sight.
Historically, protectors eventually become occupiers if left unchecked.
Keep their vigilance focused outward, friend.
The archive watches with keen interest how long this balance lasts.

moral_event_patrol_defense.journal_entry: A Peacekeeper patrol has taken position at my shelter perimeter. Captain's orders. They've got the east approach covered from dusk to dawn.

moral_event_legend_positive.event_description: Fires when moral score overflows above +200 (clamped). The player has become a legend — the wasteland mythologizes them.

peacekeeper_dialogue.speaker: Peacekeeper Captain Osa
lines: I have to be honest with you about something uncomfortable.
You're not a person to most of them anymore. You're a story. Stories don't eat, don't bleed, don't fail.
That's dangerous. For you, and for them. When the story fails — and it will, because you're human — the fall is longer.
I'll keep supporting you. But I wanted you to hear it from someone who still sees the person.

raider_dialogue.speaker: Veteran raider captain
lines: The settlers talk about you like you're some kind of miracle.
I've seen saints before. Usually they die first when the winter turns harsh.
Still, my people give your convoys a wide berth these days.
Nobody wants to be the one who shot down the wasteland's good omen.

knowledge_keeper_dialogue.speaker: Archivist primus
lines: We have opened a dedicated ledger for your deeds.
Few figures in the century since the strike have unified disparate camps in song.
Whether you intended to become a myth or not, the survivors needed one.
We will preserve your chronicle exactly as the witnesses speak it.

civilian_dialogue.speaker: Camp elder
lines: I tell the children about you. Not as a person — as a lesson.
'Be like that one,' I say. 'Give when it costs. Listen when it hurts. Stay when it's easier to go.'
You don't have to be perfect. You just have to keep being you.
But they expect perfection now. Just... know that.

civilian_dialogue.speaker: Young survivor
lines: I named my daughter after you. I hope that's okay.
She's three months old. She'll grow up hearing what you did.
I just wanted you to know that. That's all.

moral_event_legend_positive.journal_entry: I've become a legend to them — a story more than a person. Captain Osa warned me about it. Someone named their child after me. The fall, when it comes, will be longer.

moral_event_legend_negative.event_description: Fires when moral score overflows below -200 (clamped). The player has become a monster in the wasteland's collective memory.

peacekeeper_dialogue.speaker: Peacekeeper Captain Osa
lines: I'm not going to waste words. You won't hear them anyway.
The bounty is now 'dead or alive.' I voted alive. I was outvoted.
If you come within visual range of any outpost, the standing order is fire. No warning. No parley.
I don't know what happened to you. I stopped trying to understand. Goodbye.

raider_dialogue.speaker: Raider warlord
lines: You. I've been watching your work.
Most of my people are afraid of you. That's useful — to a point.
Past that point, you become a problem I have to solve instead of use.
So here's the arrangement: you stay south of the river, I stay north. We don't cross paths.
Cross the river, and I'll put fifty guns on you. Not because I hate you — because you're too dangerous to let roam.

knowledge_keeper_dialogue.speaker: Senior archivist, voice trembling
lines: Your file has been transferred to the closed index of catastrophic threats.
We do not erase history, but we do warn the future about what walk among us.
Take what you will from the ruins, but do not set fire to the knowledge within.
Even monsters should leave the books alone.

civilian_dialogue.speaker: Camp mother, whispering to children
lines: Shh. Be quiet now.
See that one? The one walking past? Don't look. Don't look at them.
If they ever come to our door, you hide. You hide and you don't make a sound.
That's what happens when someone stops being a person. Remember that.

moral_event_legend_negative.journal_entry: The Peacekeepers changed the bounty to 'dead or alive.' The raider warlord drew a line at the river — south is mine, north is theirs. Mothers tell their children to hide when I pass. I've become the thing they warn about.
